newsitem.title: FRANCE: Forecasts show French growth consensus - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Forecasts show French growth consensus - ministry.

text.p: French growth and deficit forecasts collated by a technical group in the national accounts auditing body largely underpin the government's own forecasts, a finance ministry official said on Thursday.

Earlier, the technical committee in the auditing body issued a sample of forecasts from eight economic research groups which showed a range of 2.0-2.5 percent for 1997 GDP growth, averaging out at 2.1 percent.
The sample showed forecasts for public deficits as a portion of GDP of between 3.0 and 3.5 percent, averaging at 3.2 percent.
"It's not an official forecast. It's a compilation of the forecasts of all these groups," said a ministry official.
"It is rare to see such a consensus and it's very close," the official added.
"What this amounts to is that there is a consensus on the acceleration in growth," the official added.
Government forecasts are for GDP growth of 2.3 percent and a public deficit of 2.9 percent of GDP next year.
